newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end mostly up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end mostly up in slow trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures traded on both sides of previous levels in thin trade but finished mostly higher on renewed short covering late, traders said.
Lumber futures closed $2.20 per thousand board feet higher to $0.70 lower with March up $2.10 at $385.60 and May up $0.90 at $380.90 per tbf. Only September posted a loss.
Futures firmed again late on short covering but the market continued to show little direction as many traders said they were awaiting fresh direction from the cash spruce market.
Rolling of positions out of March now that it is spot added to uneven trade at times, they said.
Refco and Griffin Trading notalby sold May early, pit sources said.
The Commerce Department reported January construction spending was up 0.4 percent to $589.8 billion with private construction at $445.7 billion, the highest on record.
